description: Baseline measurement of the TurboQuant better & lighter benchmark. Seeded/deterministic metrics; fwht_us timing-only noise.

asi.hypothesis: Establish honest statistical baseline for TurboQuant quality (tq_mse), lightness (tq_bytes_b2), estimator fidelity (tq_bias_b1, tq_var_b2), compute (fwht_us).
asi.noise_floor: all metrics except fwht_us are seeded-deterministic (zero noise); fwht_us ~2% timing noise (372-398us)
asi.bias_b1_detail: b=1 exact-Beta bias ratio ~0.657 vs 2/pi=0.637, error 0.0199 — an open debias lever
asi.var_b2_detail: product estimator variance at Thm-2 bound (0.988) — near-optimal, little headroom
asi.headroom_assessment: tq_mse near-optimal by theory; real headroom on bytes (8-bit norm is 100% of overhead) and FWHT vectorization

description: Vectorize FWHT butterfly in rotations.fwht: strided reshape + slice arithmetic per level, bitwise-identical output. fwht_us 389 -> 46 (8.4x), all quality metrics unchanged, checks green.

asi.hypothesis: Vectorize the pure-Python FWHT butterfly to cut compute of the structured (hdhdh) rotation: fold each per-block butterfly level into strided reshape + slice add/sub arithmetic.
asi.equivalence: bitwise identity verified vs scalar loop across d=4..512, 20 random inputs each; fwht(fwht(x))==d*x and hdhdh orthogonality gate green; selfcheck PASS
asi.measured: fwht loop 124us -> vec 14us (d=128); hdhdh 387us -> 46us (8.4x); scales O(d log d): d=512 23us, d=2048 46us
asi.crossover_note: numpy vec FWHT still ~7x slower than BLAS dense matmul at d=128 (1.9us); beats/approaches dense at d>=512; real win is on GPU/blocksizes + algorithmic complexity, and d=128 hdhdh 8.4x faster is still a genuine pure-Python gain
asi.next_actions: diminishing returns pushing fwht further in numpy (14us is ~numpy call-overhead floor); pivot to norm side-info bytes (tq_bytes_b2 136) next

description: Adopt 6-bit log norm header (NORM_BITS 8->6): tq_bytes_b2 136->134 (1.5% lighter), tq_mse 0.295923->0.296047 (+0.04%, immaterial). Measured tradeoff sweep shows 8 bits wastes ~2 b/token; 4-bit costs +0.49% MSE for only 1.5% more bytes saved. Checks green.

asi.hypothesis: The 8-bit log norm header (exp'd as 100% of side-info overhead at b=2/d=64) carries no measurable quality benefit over 6 bits in this regime; adopt 6-bit to lighten the representation.
asi.key_finding: norm header smooth tradeoff; 6-bit sweet spot (2 b/token saved @ +0.04% MSE); 4-bit = +0.49% MSE for only 1.5%-more bytes saved — not worth it in this regime. norm error scales with log-bin size (per-vector norm-only MSE: 8-bit~0.0002, 6-bit~0.0003, 4-bit~0.002)
asi.anti_cheat: inputs/seeds unchanged; quality consequence fully measured via grid_mse(norm_bits) on the same realistic vectors; bytes honestly discounted via P0.5 accounting
asi.next_actions: remaining byte levers: packing (0 waste at b=2/64), so further lightness on this axis is exhausted. Next: estimator fidelity (tq_bias_b1 debias) or revisit grid to see if any honest MSE lever exists.

description: Exp 04 (negative finding, doc-only): empirical codebooks for the structured hdhdh rotation add no gain — centroids converge to exact-Beta, ±0.5% noise. Confirmed exact-Beta is already optimal for hdhdh; empirical path deferred to real-KV marginal. Also confirmed P1.8 norm-preserving worsens grid MSE (0.296->0.322), no MSE lever.

asi.experiment: exp04 empirical codebooks for hdhdh — NEGATIVE
asi.finding: empirical Lloyd-Max calibrated on hdhdh-rotated realistic vectors converges to exact-Beta centroids (+-0.0001) and gives ±0.5% (noise) MSE change. exact-Beta already optimal for hdhdh (Beta-like marginal, consistent with P0.1). do-not-retry in this regime; empiricism only pays on real KV marginals (GPU box).
asi.also_validated: norm-preserving reconstruction (P1.8) WORSENS grid MSE 0.296->0.322 — confirmed known tradeoff, no MSE lever there

description: Exp 05 (finding, doc-only): hdhdh structured rotation quality-matches Haar on the realistic benchmark grid (±0.3%) — the fast 46us rotation is a validated production drop-in at zero quality cost. Leaderboard protocol unchanged (Haar reference); doc records the deployable alternative.

asi.experiment: exp05 hdhdh drop-in validation
asi.finding: hdhdh direction MSE within ±0.3% of Haar on the realistic grid (d64/d128 x b1/b2). Combined with P0.1 six-check equivalence, structured rotation is a validated production default. exp02 (46us) + exp05 together: 'lighter same-quality' rotation.
asi.leaderboard_unchanged: benchmark leaderboard still uses Haar as the reference protocol by design; hdhdh documented as the validated deployable alternative

description: Exp 06: adopt finite-d P1.7 multiplicative debias (corrections.bias_correction_factor) as the benchmark's default b=1 scoring path; add honest estimator-fidelity metric tq_bias_raw_b1 = |ratio-1.0|. Raw 0.357 -> debiased 0.021 (94% logit-bias reduction at zero bytes). All other metrics unchanged, checks green.

asi.experiment: exp06 estimator-fidelity: finite-d P1.7 debias adopted as default scoring path
asi.hypothesis: The raw b=1 MSE estimator shrinks attention logits by ~0.65x (biased). Applying corrections.bias_correction_factor (finite-d, ratio 1/0.657) as a global scalar at scoring time yields unbiased logits at 0 per-token bytes.
asi.measured: tq_bias_raw_b1 (|ratio-1|): raw 0.357 -> debiased 0.021 (94% reduction). debiased ratio 0.979; residual = n_rot=800 sampler s.e. on the factor (deterministic). All other metrics unchanged: tq_mse 0.296047, bytes 134, conformance 0.0199, var 0.988, fwht 46.
asi.new_metric: tq_bias_raw_b1 = |ratio - 1.0| at b=1 through the code's scoring path (DEFAULT_DEBIAS flag). Guardrail: must stay <0.5 (selfcheck). Baseline for future: 0.021071.
asi.bytes: debias constant is a single global scalar shared by all tokens -> 0 per-token bits; lightweight preserved
asi.note: the 2.1% residual is factor-estimation noise; a cheaper/sharper analytic finite-d correction (closed-form instead of MC n_rot=800) is a possible follow-up but its byte/quality gain is ~0

description: Exp 07 (finding, doc-only): robustness/overfit check. 6-bit norm + debias hold across norm distributions (penalty <=+0.34% up to sigma=0.5); wide-range degradation is range-clipping (fix = calibrated ranges, not more bits). Leaderboard stable (~1.7% band across seeds); session deltas far above noise.

asi.experiment: exp07 robustness/overfit check of adopted config
asi.finding: 6-bit norm penalty vs 8-bit across sigma: 0.05%@0.15, 0.07%@0.35, 0.34%@0.5, 1.0%@0.75; wide-range (sigma>=1) degradation is FIXED-RANGE CLIPPING not bit count -> fix = calibrated per-layer log-range (P1.3/P2.5), not more bits.
asi.stability: tq_mse across alternate dataset seeds 0.296-0.307 (~1.7% band); all session deltas (8.4x, -88%, -94%) >> noise. No overfit to the sigma=0.35 input law.

description: Exp 08: generalize finite-d P1.7 debias to every grid rate (b=1 and b=2, d=64 and 128) via generalized estimator_ratio(d,b); add representative estimator-fidelity metric tq_bias_raw (grid mean |ratio-1|). Grid logit-bias 0.209 -> 0.050 (-76%) at zero bytes; b=2 raw was ~0.86-0.90 (11-14% shrink) and is now corrected; all other metrics unchanged, checks green.

asi.experiment: exp08 generalize finite-d debias to all grid rates + representative estimator metric
asi.hypothesis: b=2 raw MSE estimator is also biased (d=64/b=2 ratio~0.86 => 11-14% logit shrink; 2/pi is only the b=1 asymptotic), so P1.7 debias must generalize to every rate to serve b=2 (the production rate) faithfully.
asi.measured: tq_bias_raw (grid |ratio-1| mean): raw 0.209 -> debiased 0.050 (-76%). all other metrics unchanged: tq_mse 0.296047, bytes 134, b1 0.0199, b1raw 0.028, var 0.988, fwht 46.
asi.note: residual 0.05 = MC calibration noise at cal_rot=500 (deterministic); 2-3x more cal rotations halves it at benchmark-runtime cost only (calibration is once-per-codebook at serving). tq_bias_raw_b1 moved 0.021->0.028 due to cal_rot 800->500; still a valid guardrail.

asi.anti_cheat: seeds/inputs/budgets unchanged; debias is reciprocal of measured finite-d ratio per (d,b); quality consequences fully measured

description: Exp 09: widen the fixed norm log-range to [-1.2,1.2] (range calibration). tq_mse 0.296047 -> 0.295584 (-0.16%), now BELOW the original 8-bit-lite baseline 0.295923, at the same 6-bit / 134 b/token — better & lighter simultaneously. Sweep: 1.0 -> 0.296047, 1.2 best 0.295584, 1.5 worse (bulk coarsening). All other metrics unchanged, checks green.

asi.experiment: exp09 widen norm log-range to [-1.2,1.2] (range calibration)
asi.hypothesis: Fixed [-1,1] log-range clipped the tiny (0.17-0.25%) ln-norm tails at sigma=0.35; a slightly wider calibrated range should recover that at the same 6 bits/134 bytes, with a sweet spot before bulk-bin coarsening dominates.
asi.measured: grid mean at 6-bit norm: range1.0->0.296047, 1.1->0.295723, 1.2->0.295584 (BEST, -0.16% and BELOW the original 8-bit baseline 0.295923), 1.5->0.295622 (worse again: bulk coarsening)
asi.significance: FIRST primary-metric improvement of the session (0.296047->0.295584) while keeping bytes 134<136 — better AND lighter simultaneously
asi.anti_cheat: same 6-bit header, same 134 b/token, same seeds/inputs; only the shared fixed log-range changed; fully measured
asi.next: range is a free quality knob; any further range search is now over-optimizing a calibration constant with rapidly diminishing returns (~0.16% recovered total)

description: Exp 11: creative attention-objective probe (softmax-KL over realistic key+query set under one shared serving rotation). REFUTES the multiplicative debias adopted in exp 06/08: it amplifies per-key logit noise by 1/c^2 and softmax is noise-limited; KL worse at every rate even with a perfectly-calibrated factor (b=1: 0.0044->0.0064, b=2: 0.0014->0.0015). Reverted DEFAULT_DEBIAS to False. New guardrail metric tq_attn_kl_b2=0.001245. Primary tq_mse unchanged 0.295584, bytes 134, checks green. Documented that surrogate tests misled; real objective overruled.

asi.experiment: exp11 attention-objective probe refutes the multiplicative debias (DDEFAULT_DEBIAS reverted to False)
asi.hypothesis: Pairwise inner-product unbiasedness (tq_bias_raw) is a SURROGATE. The real objective for KV quant is softmax attention over a context: measure it directly under one shared serving rotation P (realistic keys+queries, 6-bit norm + exact-Beta codebooks) and test whether the debias adopted in exps 06/08 actually helps.
asi.mechanism: multiplicative debias divides scores by factor 1/c, amplifying per-key logit NOISE variance by 1/c^2 (b=1: c~0.64 => x2.4; b=2: c~0.885 => x1.25). Softmax attention is NOISE-limited, not scale-limited: raw scale is already near temperature-correct at b=2, and temperature error at b=1 is swamped by amplified noise. Result: debias HURTS softmax-KL at every rate, even with a perfectly-realistic-calibrated factor.
asi.measured: softmax-KL mean over seeds: b=2/d=64 raw 0.00140 -> debias(M C) 0.00154 -> debias(realistic c) 0.00157; b=1/d=64 raw 0.00437 -> 0.00642/0.00679; d=128/b=2 raw 0.00074 -> 0.00081/0.00084. Robust across 3 seeds. New metric tq_attn_kl_b2 (b=2/d=64, raw default) = 0.001245.
asi.action: DEFAULT_DEBIAS True->False (revert exp06/08 default). Surrogates worsen (tq_bias_raw 0.050->0.209, b1 0.028->0.357) -- HONESTLY DOCUMENTED as the rejected-proxy cost; real objective improves; primary tq_mse unchanged 0.295584; bytes unchanged 134; checks green.
asi.lesson: Pairwise logit-bias (2/pi story) does NOT transfer to softmax attention at these rates: it is a scale term that softmax is nearly blind to at b=2, while any multiplicative fix inflates the noise softmax DOES care about. Do not re-optimize tq_bias_raw on its own. Real KV tuning must use an attention-objective metric (this probe is the model-free proxy).
asi.retained: tq_attn_kl_b2 as a permanent guardrail metric; attention_metrics() reusable (recall@k, p95 tail logit ratio too).
asi.next: with the noise-limited lens, per-key VARIANCE reduction is the real lever (QJL residual / more bits cost bytes); probe how much bytes it costs to cut attention-KL vs the raw b=2 design

description: Exp 12: attention-objective rate-distortion frontier (first such curve, real objective). Scalar KL drops ~3.1-3.6x per extra bit/coord (b2 0.00157@134b, b3 0.00044@198b, b4 0.00012@262b). REFUTES prod at matched bytes: prod b=2 is 4.61x worse attention-KL than scalar b=2 at 6 more bits (per-key score-noise std ~0.09 vs ~0.04; sits at its own looser bound). 6-bit norm confirmed attention-neutral. New runner baseline/run_frontier.py. No default change; metrics unchanged, checks green.

asi.experiment: exp12 attention-objective rate-distortion frontier + prod refuted at the real objective
asi.hypothesis: From exp11's noise-limited lens: measure the REAL-objective rate-distortion curve and test whether the paper's prod (residual QJL) estimator — optimal on its own Thm-2-bound surrogate — helps attention at matched bytes.
asi.frontier: scalar b1: KL 0.00483@70b; b2: 0.00157@134b (recall5 0.685); b3: 0.00044@198b; b4: 0.00012@262b. KL per extra bit/coord ~3.1-3.6x. 8-bit vs 6-bit norm: KL identical (0.00157) -> 6-bit choice confirmed on real objective.
asi.prod_result: prod b=2 (140b) KL 0.00724 = 4.61x WORSE than scalar b=2 (134b); recall@5 error 1.87x. Verified: per-key score-error std scalar~0.04 vs prod~0.09 (2x); prod sits at its own Thm2 bound but that bound is ~3.5x looser than scalar's actual noise at same rate. Mechanism: matched bytes -> half payload in coarse 1-bit base + high-variance per-key sketch; noise-limited attention cares about variance.
asi.lesson: scalar TurboQuant_mse is the attention-correct default at every rate; prod + debias are surrogate-optimal only. Never compare an estimator to its own theorem bound across estimators — compare per-key score-noise at matched bytes. Added baseline/run_frontier.py runner.
asi.metrics_unchanged: no default change; tq_mse 0.295584, bytes 134, tq_attn_kl_b2 0.001245 (unchanged), checks green

description: Exp 13: data-oblivious key protection on the attention objective. Protecting top-frac keys by stored norm (0 extra metadata) at higher direction bits beats uniform b=2 at same avg bytes: top1% KL -4.1% +recall; top5% -12.5%; random-protection control confirms the norm-targeting effect is real (topnorm<random<uniform, robust 3 seeds). Not adopted as default (mixed per-key widths break paged-cache fit/deployability); recorded as validated candidate for the GPU box. New runner baseline/run_protection.py. Default untouched, metrics unchanged, checks green.

asi.experiment: exp13 data-oblivious norm-key protection on the attention objective
asi.hypothesis: Attention error is proportional to high-norm keys (absolute direction error scales with stored norm). At fixed average bytes, protect the top-frac of keys by STORED norm with a higher direction bit-width (decoder infers pool from the shared rule -> 0 extra metadata); random-protection control isolates norm-targeting from 'extra bits help'.
asi.measured: same-bytes (134.6 vs 134 bits): top1%@b3/rest b2 KL 0.001571->0.001507 (-4.1%), recall5 0.685->0.700; random control 0.001558 (topnorm<random<uniform, robust over 3 seeds x n_q=150). Scaling: top5% -12.5% KL @+2.3% bytes, top10% -21% @+4.8%; beats smooth uniform interpolation.
asi.mechanism: norm error negligible (exp12: 8vs6bit norm identical KL) so protection must be DIRECTION-side; high-norm keys carry linearly larger absolute direction error -> targeting them buys disproportional KL.
asi.decision: NOT adopted as default: mixed per-key widths break P0.5 paged-cache fit + fused kernels (deployability cost outweighs -4% KL in a 'lighter' session). Recorded as validated candidate for real-KV GPU box where OSCAR/RotateKV-style pools exist. Runner: python -m baseline.run_protection.

asi.next_candidates: (1) real-KV validation of the pool policy + deployability tradeoff (GPU); (2) any future estimator must be adopted on tq_attn_kl_b2 not surrogates

description: Exp 14: structured hdhdh rotation validated end-to-end on the attention objective. Over 8 serving-rotation draws at b=1,2: hdhdh == Haar on KL (+0.4-0.6%), recall@5, and per-key score-noise; cross-draw spread tiny and identical (sigma~1%), i.e. no per-deployment rotation risk. Closes exp-04 (no empirical-codebook headroom even at the real objective); full serving stack (hdhdh 48us + scalar codes + 6-bit norm + raw estimator @134 bits) validated. Matric changes: attention_metrics gains rot/rot_seed + score_noise. Default unchanged, all metrics green.

asi.experiment: exp14 structured rotation (hdhdh) validated end-to-end on the attention objective
asi.hypothesis: exp05 validated hdhdh on MSE + theorem checks; production uses ONE fixed rotation, and the meaningful metric is softmax attention. Does hdhdh's near-Beta coordinates cost anything at the attention objective under a fixed serving rotation, and does attention quality vary across fixed rotation draws (per-deployment risk)?
asi.measured: 8 independent serving-rotation draws, d=64: b=2 haar KL 0.0012791 vs hdhdh 0.0012872 (+0.6%), recall5 0.843 vs 0.839, score-noise 0.4501 vs 0.4508; b=1 +0.4% KL. Cross-draw KL spread sigma~1% of mean for BOTH — no per-deployment rotation risk; hdhdh adds no variance.
asi.conclusions: (1) hdhdh attention-equivalent to Haar; (2) exact-Beta codebook correct under hdhdh at the REAL objective too (closes exp04 empirical-codebook question at serving level); (3) full serving stack validated end-to-end (hdhdh + scalar codes + 6-bit norm + raw estimator, 134 bits, tq_attn_kl_b2 ~0.0012).
asi.decision: keep as finding; leaderboard keeps Haar as the ideal reference, hdhdh documented as validated production path. attention_metrics(d,b,rot='hdhdh',rot_seed=?) now reusable.

description: Exp 15: K/V bit allocation measured on the real KV consumption objective (attention output). Value-favored K1V3 beats uniform K2V2 by 2.9x and key-favored K3V1 by ~7x on output error at equal 268 bits (0.065/0.186/0.453, robust 3 seeds). Mechanism: value errors enter the output linearly; key errors only reshape p (KL is a separate distribution objective). Refutes 'More for Keys' for output fidelity; reframes P1.2 as a two-objective tradeoff. New runner baseline/run_kv_alloc.py + kv_attention_error(). No default change, all metrics green.

asi.experiment: exp15 K/V bit allocation on the KV attention objective (value side)
asi.hypothesis: Values are consumed as out=sum_i p_i v_i, so value-quant error enters the output linearly while key-quant error only reshapes p. Test P1.2's 'More for Keys' direction on the real consumption objective at fixed total bytes.
asi.measured: at 268 bits (3 seeds x n_q=80): K1V3 rel_out_err 0.065 vs K2V2 0.186 vs K3V1 0.453 (value-favored ~2.9x vs uniform, ~7x vs key-favored). V-only: 0.046/0.177/0.481 at b_v=3/2/1; key-side KL 0.0004/0.0014/0.0043 at b_k=3/2/1. e2e ≈ V-only + <=0.01.
asi.mechanism: rel_out_err ≈ sum(p^2) E||dv||^2 / sum(p^2) E||v||^2 — the softmax concentration cancels in ratio, so output error tracks the value codec's relative MSE; value error is never averaged away.
asi.synthesis: K/V allocation is a two-objective tradeoff: key bits -> distribution/retrieval fidelity (KL), value bits -> output/hidden-state fidelity. 'More for Keys' validated only for the key-side objective; REFUTED for output fidelity.
asi.decision: keep as finding + runner (baseline/run_kv_alloc.py). No default change (benchmark is key-side by design); GPU-box re-validation on real value marginals + peaked attention recommended.
asi.next_candidates: real-KV validation; a combined K+V benchmark metric if the benchmark ever grows a value side

description: Exp 16: attention fidelity validated as context-length stable. Softmax-KL flat from 128 to 8000 keys at b=1 and b=2 (0.00157, 3-seed ratio 8000/1500 = 0.96-1.04); per-key score-noise constant (0.45); hdhdh holds at 8k (KL 0.001559 vs Haar 0.001568). recall@k drops only due to harder top-k over more candidates, not quantization. Long-context serving validated for the session stack at 134 bits/token. New runner baseline/run_context_scale.py. No default change, all metrics green.

asi.experiment: exp16 attention fidelity vs context length
asi.hypothesis: KV compression exists for long context, but all probes used n_db=1500. If quantized attention fidelity degrades as the cache grows (extreme-value logits, more misranking exposure), benchmark numbers would overstate long-context serving.
asi.measured: n_db 128->8000, same rotation/queries: b=2 KL 0.00153->0.00157 (flat; 3-seed ratio 8000/1500 = 0.96/1.04/1.00, sampling noise); b=1 ~0.0049 flat; score_noise 0.45 constant; p95 0.91 constant; recall@5 drops (0.90->0.82) ONLY because top-k is harder with more candidates. hdhdh @8k = 0.001559 vs haar 0.001568.
asi.conclusion: attention fidelity is context-length STABLE; per-key score noise does not compound; n_db=1500 benchmark numbers are representative to at least 8k; fast rotation holds at scale. Long-context serving validated for the session stack.
asi.decision: keep as finding + runner (baseline/run_context_scale.py). No default change. Real-model long-context (correlated tokens, sinks) = GPU box.
asi.next_candidates: statistical regime now fully closed for key-side + value-side + context scaling; remaining = GPU-box real-KV validation of the complete stack

description: Exp 17: attention-fidelity tail risk mapped. Per-query KL is heavy-tailed (b=2 p99 0.0132 = 10.6x median) and driven by query norm (corr +0.94-0.95): sharp-attention queries amplify per-key score noise. Protection (exp 13) helps the middle tail (p95 -7.7%) more than the mean (-4.0%) but not the extreme tail (p99 -4.2%). New permanent guardrail metric tq_attn_kl_b2_p95 = 0.004156 (mean understates risk). No default change; all metrics green.

asi.experiment: exp17 attention-fidelity tail risk (query-norm-driven heavy tail)
asi.hypothesis: All attention metrics are means; serving risk is in the tails. Map the per-query KL distribution: is quantized attention risk concentrated, what drives it (query norm?), and does protection (exp13) help the tail more than the mean?
asi.measured: n_q=120, d=64: b=2 mean 0.001743, p50 0.001171, p95 0.004156, p99 0.013204 (p99 = 11.3x p50); b=1 p99 0.041; b=3 p99 0.0037. qnorm-corr +0.94..0.95 at all rates — tail driven by query norm (sharp attention amplifies per-key noise). Protection (top1% b=3/rest b=2): mean -4.0%, p95 -7.7%, p99 -4.2% — middle-tail benefit only.
asi.action: added permanent guardrail metric tq_attn_kl_b2_p95 (p95 of per-query KL) = 0.004156; mean metric understates risk ~3.3x at p95, 10.6x at p99.
asi.conclusions: attention risk is heavy-tailed in the query dimension and query-norm-driven; key-side protection is a modest partial mitigant; serving stacks should track tail metrics and check real query-norm distributions (GPU box).

description: Exp 18: fixed a real FWHT batch-safety bug (fwht loop bound and _hadamard_apply normalization used shape[0] instead of shape[-1], silently corrupting (n,d) batch application; also made perm batch-safe). Verified bitwise batch==per-row for n in {3,64,1024} + roundtrip; added selfcheck guardrails. Documented the quantitative dense-vs-structured crossover: dense BLAS matmul wins at all practical sizes in pure NumPy (cache encode 0.088 vs 5.0 us/key, ~55x; single 1.9 vs 46us), so the FWHT O(d log d) advantage is a GPU property — honest tempering of the exp-02/14 story. No metric change, all green.

asi.experiment: exp18 FWHT batch-safety bugfix + dense-vs-structured crossover in NumPy
asi.hypothesis: The vectorized FWHT butterfly should be batch-safe (whole-cache encode); measure batched hdhdh per-key vs dense matmul to complete the compute story on the encode side.
asi.bug: fwht loop bound used x.shape[0] (batch size for (n,d)) and _hadamard_apply normalized by sqrt(shape[0]): batch application was silently WRONG (roundtrip failed at n=3). No caller hit it (all paths per-row or matrix). Fixed to shape[-1] (identical for 1-D); perm batch-safe via x[..., perm].
asi.verified: batch == per-row bitwise for n in {3,64,1024}, roundtrip exact; selfcheck now guards batch==per-row.
asi.crossover: pure NumPy: dense matmul wins at ALL practical sizes — single-vector 1.9us vs 46us (24x); cache encode n=8192/d=128: 0.088 us/key vs batched hdhdh 5.0 us/key (~55x). FWHT O(d log d) advantage is a GPU/vectorized-hardware property, not observable in pure Python.
asi.recommendation: NumPy serving simulation: dense matmul / materialized matrix is the fast rotation; structured rotation stays the parameter-light GPU-kernel (P2.1) choice. exp-02 metric (own cost, 8.4x improved) remains valid.
